concerns.text: McNemar’s exact test is applied to the paired binary outcomes across all 5 seeds per task (120 paired observations). McNemar’s test assumes a single paired observation per subject; the repeated‑measure structure (multiple seeds) violates the independence assumption and can inflate Type I error. The plan should either aggregate per‑task outcomes (e.g., majority vote) before applying McNemar, or use a statistical model that accounts for within‑task correlation (e.g., mixed‑effects logistic regression).

A paired t‑test is proposed as a secondary exploratory analysis on binary success/failure data. The t‑test assumes continuous, approximately normally distributed differences, which is not satisfied for binary outcomes. A more appropriate alternative would be a Wilcoxon signed‑rank test or a logistic mixed‑effects model. Using the t‑test may lead to misleading effect‑size estimates.
